Definition: a little or few (often adverbial or compar.)
BiblicalUsage: A little is the small amount, and the Bible uses it to measure what matters: better is little with the fear of the LORD than great treasure with trouble, and better is a little with righteousness than great revenues without right. The widow of Zarephath has only a little meal in the barrel, and Abraham asks for a little water to wash the angels' feet.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that little with God is more than much without Him: the widow's little meal fed three people through a famine, and the proverb says the same in a sentence — a little with the fear of the LORD is enough.
